newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian liquidity seen tight for next few years.
newsitem.headline: Indian liquidity seen tight for next few years.

text.p: Indian companies should be prepared to live with a liquidity shortage for two more years, Bhagirath Merchant, a leading broker and former president of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Friday.

"Tight liquidity is here to stay for the next one or two years," Merchant told a business conference. Indian industrialists and industry associations had branded 1995/96 (April-March) as a year of liquidity crunch.
Merchant said Indian financial institutions were lending money at over 20 percent per annum and wondered how viable would be new projects financed at such high costs.
He doubted if Indian capital markets could generate the resources to fund the current 12 percent industrial growth over the next five to 10 years.
He said an increase in savings rate was unthinkable given the rising consumerism triggered by penetration of television in rural India.
S.S. Tarapore, the deputy governor of the Reserve Bank of India, who spoke earlier, said the funds shortage was over.
"The liquidity crunch which preoccupied the industry in 1995/96 has all but disappeared and money market rates have been low for a number of months," Tarapore said.
